sec: Laron dwarfism, provocative testing and acromegaly etiology

items.q: A 7-year-old child presents with severe dwarfism and craniofacial disproportion. Biochemical evaluation demonstrates elevated circulating growth hormone with profoundly low levels of IGF-1 and IGFBP-3. This condition is caused by:
items.exp: Laron dwarfism is caused by an inactivating GHR mutation; GH is elevated but downstream IGF-1 and IGFBP are markedly decreased. (Book p947)

items.q: In Laron dwarfism, mutated GHR leads to low IGF-1 and low insulin, which causes an increase in nuclear ___ transcription factors.
items.exp: Mutated GHR in Laron dwarf leads to decreased IGF-1/insulin and elevated nuclear FoxOs. (Book p947)

items.q: Which dynamic provocative investigation serves as the gold standard test to evaluate suspected growth hormone deficiency?
items.exp: The insulin tolerance test (inducing hypoglycemia) is the gold standard provocative test for GH deficiency. (Book p947)

items.q: Match the dynamic provocative GH test to its current clinical status — 1) Insulin tolerance test 2) Glucagon-mediated stimulation 3) Arginine, Clonidine, L-Dopa, GHRH … A) Standard provocative test B) Recognized provocative test C) Other stimulation tests no longer in active use
items.exp: ITT and glucagon stimulation are active provocative tests; arginine, clonidine, L-dopa, and GHRH are obsolete tests not in routine use. (Book p947)

items.q: What percentage of acromegaly cases are caused by a primary GH-secreting pituitary adenoma?
items.exp: Pituitary gland adenomas account for 98% of all cases of acromegaly. (Book p947)

items.q: What proportion of somatomammotropin adenomas causing acromegaly contain co-expressed lactotrophic cells?
items.exp: Somatomammotropin adenomas causing acromegaly contain lactotroph cells in 20% of cases. (Book p947)

items.q: A 48-year-old female presents with signs of acromegaly. Pituitary MRI is completely normal, but abdominal CT reveals a functional neuroendocrine tumor. Ectopic authentic GH secretion is classically caused by:
items.exp: Ectopic growth hormone secretion is a classical finding in pancreatic islet cell tumors. (Book p947)

items.q: Match the ectopic source to the hormone it hypersecretes in acromegaly — 1) Pancreatic islet cell tumor 2) Bronchial carcinoid / small cell lung cancer … A) Direct ectopic GH secretion B) Ectopic GHRH secretion
items.exp: Pancreatic islet cell tumors classically secrete ectopic GH; bronchial carcinoid and small cell lung cancer secrete ectopic GHRH. (Book p947)

items.q: Which neoplasm is NOT recognized as a source of ectopic GHRH hypersecretion causing acromegaly?
items.exp: Ectopic GHRH is secreted by bronchial carcinoid, small cell lung cancer, and medullary carcinoma of the thyroid; adrenal carcinoma does not secrete GHRH. (Book p947)

items.q: In the hypothalamus, autonomous secretion of GHRH causing acromegaly can arise from a ___.
items.exp: Hypothalamic hamartomas can secrete excess GHRH causing secondary acromegaly. (Book p947)

items.q: Assess GH provocative testing in suspected deficiency: I Insulin tolerance test acts by inducing hypoglycemia to provoke counter-regulatory GH release. II Baseline random serum GH alone is sufficient to exclude GH deficiency.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: ITT triggers counter-regulatory GH secretion via hypoglycemia; random baseline GH is uninformative due to pulsatility. (Book p947)

items.q: What initial laboratory biomarker provides the most accurate indirect evaluation of integrated 24-hour GH activity?
items.exp: Serum IGF-1 provides an indirect integrated evaluation of growth hormone activity. (Book p947)
